page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 20 shared vCPUs and a system memory allocation of 256.0 GB RAM, which equates to 12.8 GB of memory per core. The server does not include any local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached for persistent data.

The defining feature of this server configuration is its integrated graphics processing hardware. It is equipped with three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM. This multi-GPU setup is designed to accelerate parallel computing tasks, machine learning workloads, and graphics rendering pipelines.

A primary architectural tradeoff of this instance is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained, CPU-heavy non-GPU workloads. Additionally, the complete absence of local storage requires users to provision network-attached storage, which can impact overall I/O latency. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high density of GPU resources and large memory footprint relative to the 20 vCPUs make it a specialized option for workloads that prioritize GPU acceleration and memory capacity over dedicated, high-performance CPU cores.

This server is configured for workloads that heavily leverage GPU parallelization and require significant system memory. Suitable applications include medium-scale machine learning model training, LLM inference, data science pipelines, video transcoding, and 3D rendering tasks.
